pre_conditions: The customer is assigned to the treatment group
Approved nudge templates with the required disclosures exist in the governed content library
flow_of_events: The forecasting team forecasts the next coincident system peak within the regulator's peak window
The dashboard drafts a nudge for each housing segment from approved templates
If the customer is a renter or has limited control, then the nudge offers only low-effort options and suggests no equipment or insulation upgrade
If the customer is a homeowner, then the nudge includes appliance and thermostat tips
Program staff review the drafted nudge and approve, modify, or pause it
If staff pause the nudge, then it is not scheduled
The dashboard schedules the approved nudge before the peak window
If the peak forecast is withdrawn before delivery, then the scheduled nudge is cancelled
The dashboard records the message version, its approval, and the triggering forecast in the audit trail
The dashboard delivers the nudge to the customer on web and mobile
The customer shifts flexible load, such as laundry, dishwashing, precooling, a modest thermostat change, or EV charging, out of the peak window
If the customer dismisses or pauses nudges, then the dashboard sends no further nudges until the customer resumes them
On the next day, the dashboard shows the customer's peak-window usage from interval data, labeled separately from the forecast-based nudge
post_conditions: The nudge, its approval, and its triggering forecast are recorded in the audit trail
The customer's response to the nudge is available for engagement measurement
non_functional: Customer-facing wording is drawn only from the approved content library
The dashboard meets WCAG 2.1 AA on mobile browsers

pre_conditions: The regulator has published the eligible season, coincident peak hours, baseline, and weather-normalization rules
flow_of_events: Program staff configure the evaluation period, segments, and peak window from the regulator's current definitions without changing code
The dashboard randomly assigns eligible customers to the treatment group or the holdout control group
The dashboard shows interventions only to treatment customers
Smart meters record 15-minute interval usage and transmit it to the utility the next day
The evaluator computes weather-normalized treatment-control differentials for kWh savings and coincident peak kW reduction
If interval data for a premise is missing, then the premise is handled according to the regulator's evaluation rules
The dashboard measures engagement and satisfaction by segment and links them to measured savings

The dashboard exports an audit-ready report with participation, engagement, evaluated kWh and kW with confidence intervals, broken down by treatment status, channel, housing type, income segment, and evaluation period
If a reported segment contains fewer households than the minimum count, then its figures are suppressed
Program staff submit the report for regulatory review
post_conditions: Evaluated savings and peak reduction are reported to the regulator
No individual household is identifiable in the report
non_functional: Reporting definitions are configurable rather than hard-coded
Individual households are not exposed in reports

uc_name: Estimate Bill and Explain Usage Increase
pre_conditions: The renter has signed in to the dashboard
Interval usage to date for the current billing cycle is available
flow_of_events: The renter opens the usage view during the billing cycle
The dashboard shows daily kWh next to daily temperature and marks days above 125% of the trailing 30-day median
The dashboard estimates the bill from usage to date and the renter's tariff and shows it before the bill is issued
The dashboard estimates the share of the increase attributable to heating from the usage-temperature correlation
If the increase does not correlate with temperature, then the dashboard attributes it to other loads
The dashboard shows actionable tips for usage the renter can control
If the usage is not controllable by the renter, then the dashboard offers only low-effort options and never recommends equipment or insulation changes
The renter cuts or defers controllable loads, such as turning the heat down when away or delaying laundry, while keeping the apartment within the comfort range when home
post_conditions: The renter knows the estimated bill before it is issued
The renter knows how much of the increase came from heating and which loads they can control
non_functional: Tips never propose a heating setpoint below the renter's comfort range

uc_name: Detect and Resolve Meter Data Discrepancies
pre_conditions: The homeowner's meter, inverter, battery, and charger data are connected to the dashboard
The homeowner has configured alert thresholds
flow_of_events: New meter interval data arrives the next day
The dashboard aligns meter, inverter, battery, and charger readings to 15-minute intervals
The dashboard checks each interval for anomalies
If a reading is absent past the delivery deadline or duplicated, then the interval is flagged as missing
If a reading is absent within the delivery deadline, then the interval is flagged as delayed
If the sources disagree or a register change is abnormal, then the interval is flagged as a mismatch
If an issue exceeds the homeowner's urgent thresholds, then the dashboard sends a push notification
If the issue is not urgent, then the dashboard records it and groups it with related issues for later review
The homeowner opens the flagged interval on web or mobile and sees its source, original values, and the check that triggered the flag
The homeowner downloads the raw interval records with quality flags as CSV and verifies them against the inverter logs
The homeowner marks the exception as resolved after verification
If corrected data arrives later, then the dashboard keeps the original readings and records the revision
post_conditions: Each discrepancy is either resolved or remains visible as unresolved
Original readings and their revisions are preserved
non_functional: Related alerts are grouped so the alert stream does not become noise

pre_conditions: Solar production, battery state of charge, and per-interval tariff rates are available to the dashboard
The battery reserve covers the forecast load from sunset until solar output next exceeds household load
flow_of_events: The dashboard aligns the solar production and household demand forecasts to 15-minute intervals
The dashboard applies the tariff rate and export credit that cover each interval
The dashboard compares the outcomes of charging the EV now, delaying it, or exporting, including battery losses and the reserve, and flags a likely surplus or shortfall
If a utility peak nudge to delay EV charging is received, then the dashboard evaluates it against the surplus forecast and the vehicle's departure time
If following the nudge would forgo surplus solar or force a costlier import later, then the dashboard shows that the nudge conflicts with charging from surplus
The homeowner applies the chosen allocation
If the homeowner charges from surplus, then the EV charges while the surplus lasts
If the homeowner follows the nudge, then EV charging is delayed out of the peak window
The inverter stores the remaining surplus in the battery while the battery is not full
If the battery is full, then the inverter exports the remaining surplus
The dashboard shows the resulting gross energy flows per 15-minute interval and attributes the source of EV charging
post_conditions: The surplus is allocated to the use the homeowner judged most valuable
The battery reserve still covers overnight and morning load
non_functional: Dashboard totals are reproducible from the raw interval readings
